descriptionChirho: The proper name Esarhaddon (אֵסַרְחַדֹּן), the Assyrian king (681–669 BCE, Akkadian Aššur-aḫu-iddina 'Ashur has given a brother') who succeeded his father Sennacherib (2 Kgs 19:37 = Isa 37:38) and resettled foreign peoples in Samaria (Ezra 4:2). The compound name was split across sense clusters during tokenization: S83614 captures the first element 'Esar-' (3x), while S83615 (2x) and S83617 (1x) capture the second element '-haddon/-chaddon.' These are not different senses but parts of a single compound proper name. Multilingual evidence confirms the unity: spa Esar-hadón, hin एसर्हद्दोन, arb أَسَرْحَدُّون, kor 에사르하돈, swa Esarhadoni.
